recommendedTextbook.title: Computer Studies for Junior Secondary Schools Book 1
recommendedTextbook.author: O. A. Bamiro, A. O. Nurudeen, M. O. Akande
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Historical Development of Computers: Early Calculating Devices
subtopics: Early counting mechanisms: Fingers, pebbles, tally marks
Mechanical calculating devices: Abacus, Napier's bones, slide rule, Pascaline calculator
Charles Babbage and the Analytical Engine (Father of Modern Computers)
objectives: Trace the evolution of computing from manual to electro-mechanical devices
State the historical contributions of Blaise Pascal and Charles Babbage
Perform basic addition using a wooden Chinese abacus

topics.topic: Generations of Electronic Computers (1st to 5th Generation)
subtopics: 1st Generation: Vacuum tubes, ENIAC, magnetic drums, machine language
4th Generation (VLSI microprocessors) & 5th Generation (Artificial Intelligence, quantum computing)
objectives: Identify the core electronic switching component for each computer generation
Compare the physical size, heat output, and speed of 1st vs 4th generation computers
List 3 contemporary real-world applications of 5th generation Artificial Intelligence

topics.topic: Classification of Computers: Type, Size and Purpose
subtopics: Classification by type of signal: Analog, digital, and hybrid computers
Classification by size and processing capability: Supercomputers, mainframes, minicomputers, microcomputers (desktops, laptops, tablets)
Classification by purpose: General-purpose vs special-purpose computers
objectives: Distinguish continuous analog signals from discrete binary digital computing
Explain why meteorological and oil exploration agencies use supercomputers
Identify examples of dedicated special-purpose microprocessors in household electronics

topics.topic: The Computer System: Hardware, Software and Peopleware
subtopics: Hardware components: System unit, input devices, output devices, secondary storage
Software: System software (operating systems) vs application software (user programs)
Peopleware: Computer professionals, operators, and end-users
objectives: Define the three interdependent pillars of a computer system
Diagram the flow of data through input, processor (CPU), output, and storage
State the responsibilities of a database administrator and a computer programmer
